corrections.critique: Strongest feature: Jump confronts the dependence claim by combining identity and arithmetic necessities with a demand for a bridge from their truth to divine presupposition. Principal limitation: The presentation treats reality's self-identity, arithmetic validity, and metaphysical independence as equivalent, leaving unspecified the semantics of possible circumstances and whether divine grounding differs from counterfactual falsity without God. Live burden: The theistic side must explain why these necessities require God without asserting dependence, while Jump must justify the transition from their indefeasibility to ontological independence and address the possibility that grounding need not make godless falsity coherently imaginable. Locked score: Relevance, responsiveness, and fairness sustain an 81, whereas compressed modal warrant, missing qualifications, and overstated necessity prevent an exceptional rating.

Strongest feature: Jump identifies an epistemic starting point: a thinker cannot believe that thinker exists while mistaken, connecting this certainty to nontheistic foundations of intelligibility. Principal limitation: The argument expands “this principle” from first-person self-verification to other thinkers, objects, plurality, and mathematics without inferences preserving its scope, so necessity outruns demonstrated warrant. Live burden: Jump must distinguish indubitable awareness of the present thinker from knowledge of mind-independent individuals and explain how either establishes arithmetic normativity, while the opposing side must show why the self-validating foothold requires divine grounding. Locked score: Central relevance and responsiveness support a 74, but unstable terminology, absent qualification, materially overstated extension, and moderate coherence and evidential support keep the move within the mixed band.
